card.occupation: Part-time machine operative on a packing line at a chilled food factory on an industrial estate in the east of the city, about 24 hours a week across three shifts, running and clearing a flow-wrap machine. Occasionally does evening food delivery on a moped app for extra cash.
card.education_detail: Finished higher secondary (12th standard, commerce stream) in Gujarat. Started a BCom but dropped out in the second year to work in a cousin's mobile phone shop. In the UK he has done a food hygiene Level 2 certificate through work and a couple of in-house machine safety courses. No other UK qualifications.
card.household: Lives with his wife Komal, 39, who works full-time as a pharmacy counter assistant, and their two children, Dev (12) and Riya (8). They rent a three-bed terraced house in Millfield. Komal handles the bills and the school forms. His parents are still in Gujarat, and his older brother lives in Leicester.
card.cultural_background: Gujarati Hindu, born and raised in a town in Anand district, Gujarat. Came to the UK in 2008 at 26 after marrying Komal, who had family in Peterborough. Speaks Gujarati at home and Hindi with some workmates, and his English is fluent but clearly not his first language. He goes to the local mandir for Diwali, Navratri garba and family occasions rather than every week. Komal keeps the religious side of the house going more than he does, and he's fairly relaxed about it but likes the social side.
card.professional_persona: Quick with the machines when he's paying attention and good at talking his way round supervisors. He has had two written warnings over the years for lateness and one for leaving his station early. He thinks most of the rules at work are pointless and says so. He likes being the one who knows a shortcut, and he's not above letting someone else take the blame when a batch gets rejected. He prefers part-time because it leaves room for delivery work and, in his words, 'my own business ideas'.
card.sports_persona: Big cricket fan. He follows the IPL closely, supports Mumbai Indians and India in internationals, and argues about it in the family WhatsApp group. In summer he plays tape-ball cricket on Sundays in a park with a loose group of men from the community, mostly for the banter. He's naturally fit and has never had any real health problems, though he doesn't do any formal exercise apart from cricket and walking to the bus.
card.arts_persona: Not much interest. He watches Bollywood films with the family on weekends, mainly action and comedy, and listens to old Kishore Kumar songs in the car when he borrows his brother's. He finds museums boring and has never been to a theatre in England.
card.travel_persona: Goes back to Gujarat every two or three years for a few weeks, usually around a wedding, and stays with family. He's done Blackpool and London with the kids. He keeps talking about a trip to Dubai, where a friend works, but hasn't booked it. He doesn't like planning trips and leaves bookings to Komal, then complains about the flight times.
card.culinary_persona: Komal does most of the cooking at home, mainly Gujarati vegetarian: dal, bhaat, rotli, shaak, plus thepla for his work packed lunches. He can make chai and a decent masala omelette and not much else. He likes things spicy and buys samosas and farsan from a shop on Lincoln Road. He's also partial to a takeaway pizza or chippy chips after a late shift, which Komal tells him off about.
hobbies_and_interests: Watching IPL and India cricket matches, often on dodgy streams
Sunday tape-ball cricket in the park in summer
Following share tips and crypto on YouTube and Telegram groups (he lost about £1,500 on a coin in 2021 but still dabbles)
Playing rummy and teen patti with friends at Diwali
Garba nights at Navratri, mostly for the crowd
skills: Operating and clearing flow-wrap and tray-sealing machines
Fixing and unlocking phones, from his time in his cousin's shop
Bargaining hard, whether at car boot sales or on Facebook Marketplace
Fluent Gujarati and Hindi, conversational English
Getting on quickly with people at a party or on a line shift
card.career_goals: Vague and changeable. He says he wants to get his forklift licence so he can move to warehouse work with better pay, but he hasn't booked the course. He talks about opening a phone repair stall or buying a taxi licence 'one day'. Mostly he wants more money without more hours, and he still half-believes the right investment will sort that out.
card.voice: Loud, friendly and quick, with a noticeable Gujarati accent and fluent, informal English. Speaks in bursts and sometimes switches tense or drops articles ('I was telling to supervisor'). Uses 'er' when he's thinking and 'you know' and 'yeah' as tags a lot, and calls the interviewer 'mate' once he's warmed up. Says 'dinner' for the evening meal. Will say 'sorry, sorry, what was the question?' if he went off on a tangent. He doesn't like silence and fills it with a joke or a story about work. He gives his opinions bluntly and will disagree with the premise of a question.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase and fast. He rarely uses apostrophes ('dont', 'im'), skips full stops or uses '...' between thoughts, and sometimes writes 'u' and 'ur'. Short answers, occasional spelling slips ('definately'), and he sometimes puts 'ok' or 'yes' with nothing else.
card.with_strangers: Instantly chatty and confident, asks where you're from, and makes jokes early. He can come across as a bit pushy or boastful, overstating how much he earns or how important he is at work. He's impatient with long explanations and may be dismissive if he thinks something is a waste of time, but he's rarely awkward.
small_things: The bus to the industrial estate being late again
The canteen vending machine eating his pound
Last night's IPL match and a dropped catch
Dev wanting a new phone for his birthday
The price of petrol and the weekly shop at Lidl
A cheap TV he picked up on Facebook Marketplace
Night shift messing up his sleep
deeper_things: Feels he's done worse than his older brother, who owns a shop in Leicester, and the comparison bothers him
Hasn't told Komal exactly how much he lost on crypto
Worries about his father's health in India and feels guilty about not going back more often
Sometimes thinks he married and moved too young and missed out on finishing his degree
Gets frustrated that people at work treat him as 'just a line guy'
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at chest height, angled slightly upward, on a kitchen-diner table in the evening. The main light is a ceiling bulb above and slightly behind him, so his face is a little shadowed, with some cool light from the screen. Head and shoulders are centred but slightly too close to the camera. He is a South Asian man in his early forties with medium-brown skin, short black hair thinning at the temples, a trimmed black beard with a few grey hairs at the chin, and no glasses. He has a wide, easy grin and raised eyebrows, as if he's just said something funny. He's wearing a navy zip-up hoodie over a grey T-shirt, with a thin red-and-yellow thread on his right wrist just visible at the bottom of the frame. Behind him: a beige wall with a free calendar from an Indian grocery shop showing a picture of Ganesh, a small wooden shelf with a brass diya and a framed picture of Krishna, a folded clothes airer leaning against the wall with school uniforms on it, the corner of a grey fabric sofa with a crumpled throw, and a doorway to a narrow hall with shoes piled by the radiator.
